title: iTARGEX analysis identifies ELG1 as a regulator of yeast transcription buffering and four protein-turnover regulators
summary: iTARGEX applied a mixture-regression model to gene-expression profiles from 1,484 single-gene deletion yeast mutants, associating transcriptomic changes with S-phase transcriptional buffering and global protein turnover. Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation. Follow-up protein-turnover measurements showed altered turnover in MRN1, UPF3, RAM1 and SSN3 deletion strains.
ai_technology: iTARGEX, a finite-mixture regression framework fitted by expectation maximization to single-gene-deletion transcriptomic data

evidence.tested: Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation.
evidence.unknown: The study used budding yeast and pre-existing deletion-mutant transcriptome profiles, followed by experiments on selected candidates. ELG1's role in S-phase transcription buffering was reproduced in a second yeast genetic background and rescued by PCNA-D150E; the protein-turnover effects concern yeast deletion strains. These results do not establish corresponding human functions.
evidence.ai_role: iTARGEX associated gene-expression profiles from deletion strains with biological traits without requiring prior gene annotations and nominated candidate regulators. The researchers then performed S-phase transcription and protein-turnover experiments to test the model-prioritized candidates, supporting ELG1's role in transcriptional buffering and altered turnover for four deletion strains.
